name: Terry Riley
hook: The composer of 'In C', whose tape-delay experiments and organ loops gave the Who's 'Baba O'Riley' half its name.
blurb: Terry Riley was born in Colfax, California, in 1935. With La Monte Young he performed 'Concert for Two Pianists and Tape Recorders' in 1959 and 1960. In Paris in the early 1960s he built the 'time-lag accumulator', a way to make music repeat and pile up on itself using two tape recorders. His 1964 piece 'In C' gives a group of players 53 short phrases, each repeated as many times as each player likes, over a steady pulse. It premiered at the San Francisco Tape Music Center on 4 November 1964, with Steve Reich among the players, and Reich's suggestion of a steady eighth-note pulse became part of the piece. Columbia recorded it in 1968, and in 1969 released his album 'A Rainbow in Curved Air', which layered fast, repeating organ patterns. Pete Townshend of the Who named 'Baba O'Riley' partly after him. The two-tape-machine delay later reached rock through Eno and Fripp's system on '(No Pussyfooting)' (1973), which Wikipedia's article on Frippertronics traces to studio systems by Riley and Pauline Oliveros.
